title: The Heart as a Pump, and the PCP Cardiac Assessment
next: Chapter 30, Lesson 2: Acute coronary syndrome and the BC chest pain protocol

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already treat chest pain: oxygen, ASA, nitroglycerin, the AED. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Understand the heart as a pump: output, preload, afterload
  2. Know how nerves and receptors drive the heart and your drugs
  3. Run a deeper cardiac assessment, including what only the PCP does

Textbook: Chapter 30, PDF pages 2526–2581
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter thirty, cardiovascular emergencies, the biggest chapter in the book. We'll take it in five lessons. As EMRs, you've all cared for chest pain patients: oxygen, ASA, nitroglycerin, and the AED ready. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you need to understand what's happening inside the chest, because your decisions depend on it. Today has three goals. First, the heart as a pump: cardiac output, preload, and afterload. Second, how nerves and receptors speed up or slow down the heart, which is the why behind your drugs. Third, a deeper cardiac assessment, including the part that only the PCP does.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第三十章：心血管急症，这是全书最大的一章，我们分五节课讲。作为 EMR，你们都处理过胸痛病人：给氧、ASA、硝酸甘油，AED 随时准备好。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你需要弄懂胸腔里正在发生什么，因为你的决定取决于它。今天三个目标：第一，心脏这台泵——心输出量、前负荷和后负荷；第二，神经和受体怎样让心跳加快或减慢，这就是你用药背后的道理；第三，更深入的心脏评估，包括只有 PCP 才做的那部分。

slides.title: Why cardiac calls matter
slides.body:
About half of heart attack deaths happen before hospital

  • Canada: about 159,000 new heart disease diagnoses a year
  • About 33,600 deaths a year; now second only to cancer
  • More women than men die of a cardiac event
  • Family history: first-degree relative, male < 55 or female < 65
  • Paramedics began as early care for heart attacks
slides.say: Why does this matter? Coronary heart disease, or CHD, is disease of the arteries that feed the heart muscle. Every year in Canada, about one hundred fifty-nine thousand people are newly diagnosed with heart disease, and about thirty-three thousand six hundred die of it. Only cancer kills more. The key number for us: about half of heart attack deaths happen before the patient reaches hospital. That's why the paramedic job was created in the first place. Remember too that more women than men die of a cardiac event, and that family history counts when a parent, sibling or child had heart disease young: a man under fifty-five, or a woman under sixty-five.
slides.sayZh: 为什么这很重要？冠心病（CHD）是供应心肌的动脉出了病变。加拿大每年约有十五万九千人新确诊心脏病，约三万三千六百人死于心脏病，致死人数仅次于癌症。对我们最关键的数字是：心梗死亡约有一半发生在病人到达医院之前。护理人员这个职业当初就是为此而设立的。还要记住，死于心脏事件的女性多于男性；家族史怎么算：父母、兄弟姐妹或子女年轻时患心脏病——男性不到五十五岁，女性不到六十五岁。

slides.title: The heart's own blood supply
slides.body:
Left mainsplits into LAD and circumflexleft ventricle, septum, part of RV
Right (RCA)right atrium and ventricleplus part of the left ventricle
NodesSA node: RCAAV node: RCA in 85–90%

Inferior MI is usually an RCA blockage: watch for slow rhythms, heart blocks and a weak right ventricle.
slides.say: The heart needs its own blood supply: the coronary arteries, which branch off the aorta just above the aortic valve. The left main artery splits into the left anterior descending, or LAD, and the circumflex. They feed the thick left ventricle, the septum between the ventricles, and part of the right ventricle. The right coronary artery, or RCA, feeds the right side and part of the left ventricle. It also supplies the SA node, the heart's natural pacemaker, and in eighty-five to ninety percent of people, the AV node. So in an inferior heart attack, usually an RCA blockage, watch for slow rhythms, heart blocks, and a weak right ventricle.
slides.sayZh: 心脏自己也需要供血，靠的是冠状动脉，它们从主动脉瓣正上方的主动脉发出。左主干分成左前降支（LAD）和回旋支，供应厚实的左心室、两心室之间的室间隔和部分右心室。右冠状动脉（RCA）供应右心和部分左心室，还供应心脏的天然起搏点 SA 结；在百分之八十五到九十的人身上，AV 结也由它供血。所以下壁心梗（通常是 RCA 堵塞）时，要警惕心率慢、传导阻滞和右心室无力。

slides.title: The pump at work: cardiac output
slides.body:
Stroke volume×Heart rate=Cardiac output
  • Normal adult: SV 60–100 mL, HR 60–100, CO 5–6 L/min
  • 70 mL × 70/min ≈ 4.9 L; same SV at 110/min ≈ 7.7 L
  • Frank-Starling: more stretch → stronger squeeze, up to a limit
  • A failing heart leans on stretch, so it enlarges
slides.say: Cardiac output is the blood one ventricle pumps in a minute: stroke volume, the blood pushed out with each beat, times heart rate. A normal adult pumps sixty to one hundred millilitres per beat, sixty to one hundred times a minute, for about five to six litres a minute. Raise the rate from seventy to one hundred ten with the same stroke volume, and output climbs from about four point nine to seven point seven litres. The Frank-Starling mechanism adds more: the more the muscle is stretched by incoming blood, the harder it squeezes, like a rubber band, up to a limit. Failing hearts rely on this stretch, which is why they enlarge.
slides.sayZh: 心输出量是一个心室每分钟泵出的血量：每搏输出量（每跳一下推出的血）乘以心率。正常成人每搏六十到一百毫升，每分钟跳六十到一百次，输出量约每分钟五到六升。每搏量不变、心率从七十升到一百一十，输出量就从约四点九升升到七点七升。Frank-Starling 机制还能再加一把力：回心血把心肌拉得越长，它收缩得越有力，像橡皮筋一样，但有上限。衰竭的心脏就靠这种拉伸撑着，所以会变大。

slides.title: Preload and afterload
slides.body:
PreloadAfterload
WhatPressure as the ventricle fillsPressure it pushes against
Set byVenous returnTight or relaxed arteries
Too highOverstretched: no extra outputMore work, more O₂ demand

Sudden rise in afterload (e.g. sudden severe hypertension) → left ventricle can't empty → sudden pulmonary edema.
slides.say: Two words you'll use your whole career: preload and afterload. Preload is the pressure in the ventricle as it fills, set by how much blood returns through the veins, like filling a balloon before you squeeze it. Afterload is the pressure the ventricle pushes against to get blood out. For the left ventricle, that's the pressure in the aorta, and it rises when the arteries tighten, like squeezing water through a narrow nozzle. More afterload means more work and more oxygen demand. And if afterload jumps suddenly, as in a sudden, severe rise in blood pressure, the left ventricle can't empty, blood backs up into the lungs, and sudden pulmonary edema follows.
slides.sayZh: 两个你整个职业生涯都会用到的词：前负荷和后负荷。前负荷是心室充盈时的压力，取决于静脉回流多少血，好比捏气球之前先往里灌水。后负荷是心室把血射出去时要对抗的压力；对左心室来说就是主动脉压，动脉一收紧它就升高，好比从很窄的喷嘴往外挤水。后负荷越高，做功越多、耗氧越多。如果后负荷突然飙升，比如血压突然急剧升高，左心室排不空，血倒灌回肺，紧接着就是突发肺水肿。

slides.q: A 74-year-old woman with long-standing high blood pressure suddenly becomes very short of breath. BP 224/126, crackles in both lungs. Which explanation fits best?
options: Her heart rate is too slow to keep up
A sudden rise in afterload: the left ventricle can't empty, so blood backs up into the lungs
Right ventricular failure pushing fluid into her ankles
slides.say: Let's check your understanding. A seventy-four-year-old woman with long-standing high blood pressure suddenly becomes very short of breath. Her blood pressure is two hundred twenty-four over one hundred twenty-six, and you hear crackles in both lungs. Which explanation fits best? A, her heart rate is too slow to keep up. B, a sudden rise in afterload: the left ventricle can't empty, so blood backs up into the lungs. C, low preload from dehydration. D, right ventricular failure pushing fluid into her ankles. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检验一下。一位七十四岁女性，多年高血压，突然非常气促，血压二百二十四比一百二十六，双肺湿啰音。哪种解释最合适？A 心率太慢跟不上；B 后负荷突然升高，左心室排不空，血倒灌回肺；C 脱水导致前负荷低；D 右心室衰竭把液体推到脚踝。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A sudden jump in the pressure the left ventricle pushes against, like this very high blood pressure, stops it from emptying, so pressure backs up into the lungs and causes sudden pulmonary edema. A is wrong because nothing here suggests a slow rate. C is wrong because low preload would not flood the lungs. D is wrong because right-sided failure backs blood up into the body's veins, causing swollen ankles and neck veins, not crackles.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。左心室要对抗的压力突然飙升（就像这么高的血压），它就排不空，压力倒灌回肺，引起突发肺水肿。A 错，这里没有任何心率慢的迹象；C 错，前负荷低不会让肺里积水；D 错，右心衰是把血倒灌进全身静脉，表现为脚踝肿和颈静脉怒张，而不是湿啰音。

slides.title: Brake, accelerator, and receptors
slides.body:
System / receptorWhat it does
Vagus (parasympathetic)Brake: slows SA node, holds back AV node
AlphaArteries constrict
Beta-1 (one heart)Faster, stronger, faster conduction
Beta-2 (two lungs)Bronchi and arteries dilate

Beta blockers (e.g. metoprolol) sit on beta receptors: the patient's own adrenaline can't fully work.
slides.say: The heart has a brake and an accelerator. The brake is the vagus nerve, part of the parasympathetic system. Its chemical, acetylcholine, slows the SA node and holds back the AV node. Pressure on the carotid sinus, straining on the toilet, or a full bladder or stomach can trigger it, which is why some people faint while bearing down. The accelerator is the sympathetic system, working through receptors. Alpha tightens the arteries. Beta-1 makes the heart faster and stronger: one heart, beta-1. Beta-2 opens the airways: two lungs, beta-2. Salbutamol is mainly beta-2, but it still often speeds the heart. And beta blockers, like metoprolol, block the patient's own adrenaline.
slides.sayZh: 心脏有刹车，也有油门。刹车是迷走神经，属于副交感神经系统，它释放的乙酰胆碱让 SA 结变慢、让 AV 结拦住多余冲动。压迫颈动脉窦、上厕所用力屏气、膀胱或胃胀满都能触发它，所以有人一用力屏气就晕倒。油门是交感神经系统，通过受体起作用：α 让动脉收紧；β1 让心跳更快更有力——一个心，β1；β2 让气道扩张——两个肺，β2。沙丁胺醇主要作用于 β2，但仍常让心跳加快。β 阻滞剂（比如美托洛尔）会挡住病人自身的肾上腺素。

slides.title: The cardiac history: ask sharper
slides.body:
Chest pain, breathlessness, fainting, palpitations, nausea, fatigue

  • Provoked by exertion? Did their own nitro help?
  • Quality: write their exact words; don't lead
  • Radiation: jaw, arm, back. Severity vs their usual angina
  • Woke up gasping (PND)? Needs pillows to breathe (orthopnea)?
  • Fainted sitting or lying down = more ominous
slides.say: Cardiac patients usually complain of chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, palpitations, nausea, or fatigue. As a PCP, sharpen every question. Was the pain brought on by exertion? Did the patient's own nitro help? Record their exact words for the quality, without leading them. Ask where it spreads, and compare it with their usual angina. For breathlessness, ask about PND, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, which means waking suddenly, gasping for air. And ask about orthopnea, breathlessness lying flat, so they sleep on pillows or in a recliner. Both point to left heart failure. Fainting while sitting or lying down is more worrying than fainting while standing.
slides.sayZh: 心脏病人常见的主诉是胸痛、气促、晕厥、心悸、恶心或乏力。作为 PCP，每个问题都要问得更准：疼痛是不是活动诱发的？病人自己含的硝酸甘油有没有用？性质要记下病人的原话，不要诱导。问放射到哪里，并和他平时的心绞痛比一比。气促要问 PND，即夜间阵发性呼吸困难——睡梦中突然憋醒、大口喘气；还要问端坐呼吸——平躺就喘，只能垫枕头或睡躺椅。这两样都指向左心衰。坐着或躺着时晕倒，比站着晕倒更令人担心。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: assessing the cardiac patient
slides.body:
BC Cardiac Chest Pain protocol + BC grading criteria

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Primary survey, incl. rapid body survey
  • O₂ to keep SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Pain history: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Baseline vital signs
  • Lungs: at least 6 points front or 6 back
  • Start transport early

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry: 9 systems (PCP only)
  • Cardiovascular and respiratory are key here
  • Skip a system −5%; miss related info −3%
  • Max 15% off; none if the patient can't answer
  • Then IV and dimenhydrinate (Lesson 2)
slides.say: Here's how assessment differs by licence. On the left is what every level does on a BC chest pain call: the primary survey with a rapid body survey, oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four or higher, a pain history using OPQRRRST or LOTARP, baseline vital signs, at least six lung points, and early transport. On the right is new for you: the functional enquiry, a quick review of nine body systems, which only PCPs do. On a cardiac call, cardiovascular and respiratory matter most. On the BC exam, skipping a system costs five percent, up to fifteen percent in total. The protocol also gives you an IV and an anti-nausea drug; that's next lesson.
slides.sayZh: 看看不同执照级别的评估有什么不同。左栏是 BC 胸痛呼叫里所有级别都做的：初级评估（含快速全身检查）、给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上、用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 问疼痛史、基线生命体征、至少听六个肺部点位、尽早转运。右栏是你的新任务：系统问诊，快速过一遍九个身体系统，只有 PCP 做；心脏呼叫里最关键的是心血管和呼吸系统。BC 考试漏掉一个系统扣百分之五，最多扣百分之十五。胸痛流程还给了你静脉通路和一种止吐药，下节课讲。

slides.q: On the BC practical exam, which part of the secondary survey is required for a PCP candidate but NOT for an EMR candidate?
options: A pain history using OPQRRRST or LOTARP
A functional enquiry of nine body systems
Listening to at least six lung points
slides.say: Time for a scope question. On the BC practical exam, which part of the secondary survey is required for a PCP candidate, but not for an EMR candidate? A, baseline vital signs. B, a pain history using OPQRRRST or LOTARP. C, a functional enquiry of nine body systems. D, listening to at least six lung points. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道执业范围题。BC 实操考试中，二次评估的哪一部分是 PCP 考生必须做、而 EMR 考生不要求的？A 基线生命体征；B 用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 问疼痛史；C 九个身体系统的系统问诊；D 至少听诊六个肺部点位。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. The BC grading criteria mark the functional enquiry as PCP only: nine systems, from general health to eyes, ears, nose and throat. Skipping a system costs five percent, up to fifteen percent in total. A, B and D are expected of every candidate, EMR or PCP. Vital signs and a pain history are in the chest pain protocol for all licence levels, and the six-point lung exam is a BC rule for everyone.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。BC 评分标准把系统问诊标为 PCP 专属：九个系统，从整体健康到眼耳鼻喉。漏一个系统扣百分之五，最多扣百分之十五。A、B、D 是所有考生都要做的，不论 EMR 还是 PCP：生命体征和疼痛史写在胸痛流程的「所有执照级别」里，六点肺部听诊是对所有人的 BC 规定。

slides.title: Medications tell the story
slides.body:
• What's prescribed, taken as directed, last dose
  • Borrowed pills, over-the-counter, herbal, recreational
  • Match each condition to a drug, and each drug to a condition
  • Heart drugs: beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, nitrates
  • Erectile dysfunction pills: ask discreetly; explain why

Unfamiliar drug? Ask the patient what it's for.
slides.say: Medications tell the story, and as a PCP you'll base drug decisions on them. Ask what's prescribed, whether they take it as directed, and when they took the last dose. Ask about borrowed pills, over-the-counter products, herbal supplements, and recreational drugs. Match each condition to a drug, and each drug to a condition; a gap is a clue. In heart patients, listen for beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, which are water pills, and nitrates. Always ask about erectile dysfunction drugs, because they interact dangerously with nitroglycerin. Patients may be embarrassed, so ask discreetly and explain why. And if you don't know a drug, ask what it's for.
slides.sayZh: 药物能讲出病人的故事，作为 PCP 你要据此做用药决定。问清开了什么药、有没有按医嘱吃、最后一次什么时候吃的；问有没有借吃别人的药、非处方药、草药保健品和消遣性药物。把每个病对上一种药、每种药对上一个病，对不上就是线索。心脏病人要留意 β 阻滞剂、ACE 抑制剂、利尿剂（也就是「排水药」）和硝酸酯类。一定要问有没有用治勃起功能障碍的药，因为它们和硝酸甘油相互作用很危险。病人可能不好意思，所以要私下问，并说明原因。遇到不认识的药，就问是治什么的。

slides.title: Vital signs with a cardiac eye
slides.body:
• Feel both radial pulses: rate, rhythm, strength
  • Pulse deficit: radial rate lower than the apical rate
  • Pulsus paradoxus: systolic drops > 10 mm Hg on inspiration
  • Pulsus alternans: strong and weak beats alternate
  • Chest pain: BP in both arms; > 20 mm Hg difference = abnormal
  • Narrow pulse pressure: cardiogenic shock, tamponade
slides.say: Your vital signs now go deeper. Feel both radial pulses for rate, rhythm, and strength; a weak, thready pulse suggests low cardiac output. A pulse deficit means you count fewer beats at the wrist than you hear over the heart. Pulsus paradoxus is a systolic drop of more than ten millimetres of mercury when the patient breathes in. Pulsus alternans is a pulse that alternates strong and weak beats. For every chest pain patient, take the blood pressure in both arms; a difference over twenty is abnormal, as in an aortic dissection, so tell the hospital. And a narrow pulse pressure suggests cardiogenic shock or cardiac tamponade.
slides.sayZh: 生命体征现在要测得更深。摸双侧桡动脉，看频率、节律和强弱；脉搏细弱提示心输出量低。脉搏短绌是指腕部数到的次数比心脏听诊听到的少。奇脉是病人吸气时收缩压下降超过十毫米汞柱。交替脉是脉搏一强一弱交替出现。每个胸痛病人都要测双臂血压，相差超过二十就不正常，比如主动脉夹层，要告诉医院。脉压变窄提示心源性休克或心包填塞。

slides.title: The physical exam: look, listen, feel
slides.body:
• Level of consciousness = brain perfusion
  • JVP: sit at 45°; normal 2–4 cm above the sternal angle
  • Chest: scars, nitro patch, coin-sized bump under a clavicle
  • Crackles: left heart failure. A wheeze may be cardiac
  • Swollen ankles or lower back: right heart failure
  • Treat the patient, not the monitor
slides.say: Start the physical exam with the level of consciousness: an alert, oriented patient means the brain is perfused and the pump is working. Check that the trachea is midline. With the patient sitting at forty-five degrees, the normal jugular venous pressure is two to four centimetres above the sternal angle. On the chest, look for scars, a nitro patch, or a bump the size of a one-dollar coin under the collarbone: a pacemaker or implanted defibrillator. Crackles suggest left heart failure, and a wheeze may be cardiac, not asthma. Swollen ankles or lower back suggest right heart failure. And treat the patient, not the monitor: very low output can stop the oximeter reading.
slides.sayZh: 体格检查先看意识水平：清醒、定向力好，说明大脑灌注够，泵还在工作。确认气管居中。病人半坐四十五度时，正常颈静脉压在胸骨角上方二到四厘米。胸部找手术瘢痕、硝酸甘油贴片，或锁骨下一块一元硬币大小的鼓包——那是起搏器或植入式除颤器。湿啰音提示左心衰；哮鸣音可能是心源性的，不一定是哮喘。脚踝或腰骶部水肿提示右心衰。还有，治病人，不治监护仪：心输出量极低时，血氧仪可能测不出读数。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: OPQRST + SAMPLE → BC: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Lungs: BC wants at least 6 points front or 6 back
  • Functional enquiry: PCP only, 9 systems, max 15% off
  • Book's atropine, dopamine, norepinephrine: not on the BC exam list
  • BC exam epinephrine: IM only (anaphylaxis, severe bronchospasm)
slides.say: Let's line up the book and BC. The book uses OPQRST and SAMPLE for the history, but BC scoring uses OPQRRRST or LOTARP for pain, so practise those. For the lungs, BC wants at least six points on the front or six on the back. The functional enquiry is PCP only: nine systems, with up to fifteen percent off if you skip it. The book's atropine, dopamine, and norepinephrine are not on the BC exam drug list; understand them, but don't plan to give them. And on the licensing exam, BC epinephrine is given only by intramuscular injection, for anaphylaxis or severe bronchospasm, never by IV push; in BCEHS, a PCP with additional training may also nebulize it for croup.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 对一对。书里问病史用 OPQRST 和 SAMPLE，但 BC 评分问疼痛用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP，要练这两个。肺部听诊 BC 要求前胸至少六个点或后背六个点。系统问诊只属于 PCP：九个系统，漏做最多扣百分之十五。书里的阿托品、多巴胺和去甲肾上腺素不在 BC 考试药物清单上，要理解，但别打算用。执照考试里，BC 的肾上腺素只做肌肉注射，用于过敏性休克或严重支气管痉挛，绝不静脉推注；在 BCEHS，受过额外培训的 PCP 还可以雾化给药治疗哮吼。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A normal heart rate on a beta blocker can hide shock
  • Wheeze + crackles + edema: think cardiac, not asthma
  • Salbutamol speeds the heart: more O₂ demand
  • BP in both arms before you settle on a heart attack
  • Low output can block the SpO₂ reading: trust your hands
  • Chest pain: vitals every 5 min; listen to the lungs again
slides.say: Now the watch-outs that are new at your level. A beta blocker can hide the fast pulse of shock, so a normal heart rate doesn't mean a normal patient. Wheezes with crackles, swollen ankles, and heart disease suggest a cardiac cause, sometimes called cardiac asthma. Salbutamol rarely helps there, and it speeds the heart and raises its oxygen demand. Take the blood pressure in both arms before you settle on a heart attack. When output is very low, the oximeter may fail, so trust your hands and eyes. And reassess: on a chest pain call, take vital signs every five minutes, and listen to the lungs again en route.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 层面新的注意事项。β 阻滞剂会掩盖休克时的心率增快，心率正常不等于病人正常。哮鸣音加湿啰音、脚踝水肿、有心脏病史，提示心源性原因，有时叫「心源性哮喘」；这时沙丁胺醇很少有用，还会加快心率、增加心肌耗氧。先测双臂血压，再下「心梗」的结论。心输出量很低时血氧仪可能测不出，要相信你的手和眼。还要复评：胸痛呼叫每五分钟测一次生命体征，途中再听一次肺。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. CO = SV × HR; preload and afterload set a sick heart's workload
  2. Receptors: alpha arteries, beta-1 heart, beta-2 lungs
  3. PCP assessment: both arms, JVP, lungs, and the functional enquiry

Next: acute coronary syndrome and the BC chest pain protocol
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: cardiac output equals stroke volume times heart rate, and preload and afterload decide how hard a sick heart works; a sudden jump in afterload can flood the lungs. Two: alpha tightens arteries, beta-1 drives the heart, beta-2 opens the lungs, and beta blockers blunt the beta effects, even the patient's own adrenaline. Three: your PCP assessment goes deeper: both pulses, both arms, neck veins, lungs, and the functional enquiry. Next lesson: acute coronary syndrome and the BC chest pain protocol. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，心输出量等于每搏输出量乘以心率，前负荷和后负荷决定病心要多卖力；后负荷突然飙升会让肺里积水。二，α 收紧动脉，β1 驱动心脏，β2 打开肺部气道；β 阻滞剂会削弱 β 效应，连病人自己的肾上腺素也不例外。三，PCP 评估要更深：双侧脉搏、双臂血压、颈静脉、肺部，以及系统问诊。下节课讲急性冠脉综合征和 BC 胸痛流程。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
